resolved_findings.reason: The odd-degree clauses need the observation that a four-group action in odd degree has a fixed point; this is not supplied by a formula derived only for even degree.
Lemma10 asserts which groups the triples generate; its route must include that asserted identification as well as the raw orbit sum.
The described maximal-residue construction is for B=1; the all-Borel rank exclusion also uses the earlier nontrivial-Borel search.
The search contains its own tests. The separate verification program actually reads the common predicate file; its dependency is preserved.
The rational series is proved directly from multiplicities, faithfulness and parity, rather than from the preceding ordered/fixed-count formulas.

mathematical_routes: The common stabilizer-fiber theorem is used in exceptional commuting triples, Suzuki fibers and maximal-residue augmentation; application-specific generation, support and geometry hypotheses remain explicit.

Finite-poset exact-support counting retains classical Burnside and Mobius inputs. Invariance is required for admissibility, not for each proper support sublevel. The field-support and divisor adapters remain actual application obligations.
The faithful-action normalizer exact sequence is present but unused in the selected output routes; no splitting is asserted and the full common paper is not shortened by this graph.

The arbitrary-Borel recognition and augmentation proofs feed the actual standalone search. Its independently implemented tests are distinguished from the common predicate file imported by final verification.

Historical arrows record the source arguments, including qualifications and repaired statements. They do not retroactively certify those arguments or transfer historical proofs into current logical routes.
